title: Measuring & drawing angles
examples: How do I read the numbers on the protractor?
What is the difference between acute and obtuse angles?
Can I measure an angle bigger than 180 degrees?

explain.say: Today we are learning to measure and draw angles. We use a special tool called a protractor for this. It helps us find the size of an angle in degrees.
Look closely at the protractor. You will see two sets of numbers going around. One scale goes up to one hundred eighty degrees. The other scale goes up to one hundred eighty degrees too.
When you measure an angle, always start at the zero mark. This zero mark is where the two lines meet at the bottom. This is your starting point for measuring.
An acute angle is a small angle. It measures more than zero degrees but less than ninety degrees. Think of a slice of pizza, that is often acute.
An obtuse angle is a wide angle. It measures more than ninety degrees but less than one hundred eighty degrees. Think of a slightly open book.

faq.q: What do the numbers on the protractor mean?
faq.a: The numbers show the size of the angle in degrees. A full circle is three hundred sixty degrees, but we usually only look at up to one hundred eighty degrees.
asks: How big is an angle in degrees?
What do the degree markings show?

faq.q: When do I use the zero mark?
faq.a: You must always line up one side of the angle with the zero mark on the protractor. This gives you a correct starting point for counting.
asks: Where should I start measuring from?
Do I always start at zero?

faq.a: A reflex angle is a very large angle. It measures more than one hundred eighty degrees but less than three hundred sixty degrees. It is the outside angle.
asks: What is bigger than a straight line angle?
How do I measure a reflex angle?

faq.q: How do I know if an angle is acute or obtuse?
faq.a: You compare it to a right angle, which is ninety degrees. If it is smaller than ninety, it is acute. If it is bigger, it is obtuse.
asks: What is the boundary between acute and obtuse?

faq.q: Can I use the protractor for angles bigger than 180 degrees?
faq.a: The standard protractor only shows up to one hundred eighty degrees. For bigger angles, you need to measure the smaller angle and subtract it from three hundred sixty degrees.
asks: What if the angle is over a straight line?
Can I measure angles bigger than 180 degrees?

facts: A right angle measures exactly ninety degrees.
An acute angle is always less than ninety degrees.
An obtuse angle is always between ninety and one hundred eighty degrees.
A straight line forms an angle of one hundred eighty degrees.

quiz.say: An angle measuring sixty degrees is called:
quiz.why: Sixty degrees is less than ninety degrees, so it is acute.

wrong.0: A straight angle measures one hundred eighty degrees.
wrong.2: Obtuse angles are bigger than ninety degrees.
wrong.3: A right angle must measure exactly ninety degrees.

quiz.say: If an angle is ninety-five degrees, what type of angle is it?
quiz.why: Ninety-five degrees is bigger than ninety but less than one hundred eighty.

wrong.0: Reflex angles are much larger than one hundred eighty degrees.
wrong.2: Acute angles must be smaller than ninety degrees.
wrong.3: A right angle must equal exactly ninety degrees.

quiz.say: An angle that measures exactly one hundred eighty degrees is:
quiz.why: One hundred eighty degrees forms a perfectly straight line.

wrong.0: Reflex angles are greater than one hundred eighty degrees.
wrong.1: A right angle is much smaller, only ninety degrees.
wrong.3: Obtuse angles are less than one hundred eighty degrees.
